research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10222 at 16 FR 2247, in the Federal Register of March 13, 1951 (PDF page 1; govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified, recorded as acceptable as original). The order is headed Executive Order 10222, Providing for Certain Transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration, is signed March 8, 1951, and its filing line reads Filed, Mar. 12, 1951. Text and inventory: three numbered paragraphs, confirmed as three clauses. Paragraph 1 transfers to the Federal Civil Defense Administration so much of the health services and special weapons defense functions of the Health Resources Office of the National Security Resources Board as relates to civil defense, to remain under the jurisdiction of the Federal Civil Defense Administrator "until further order of the President." Paragraph 2 transfers the related property and records of the Board, and the personnel of the Health Resources Office engaged primarily in those functions, as the Board's Chairman and the Administrator jointly determine. Paragraph 3 reads "This order shall be effective as of March 4, 1951." Ending: Executive Order 12919, National Defense Industrial Resources Preparedness, signed June 3, 1994 and printed at 59 FR 29525 in the Federal Register of June 7, 1994 (held govinfo text layer), provides in section 904(a) that "The following are superseded or revoked:" and lists as item (2) "Executive Order No. 10222 of March 8, 1951 (16 FR 2247)". Neither section 904 nor any other part of that order states an effective date, so the end is dated on signing, 1994-06-03; this is a reading, disclosed for the reviewer, and the publication date of June 7, 1994 is not used. The machine U.S. Code search found the editorial note under 42 U.S.C. 5195 that records the same revocation by section 904(a)(2) of Executive Order 12919. Unnamed earlier candidates, disclosed under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on unnamed instruments: the editorial note printed with this order in the held OFR 1989 Codification (jobs/ofr-codification-1989/output/texts/EO_10222.txt) says that Reorganization Plan No. 1 of 1958 terminated the Federal Civil Defense Administration, effective July 1, 1958, and consolidated its functions into the Office of Defense and Civilian Mobilization, and that Executive Order 10952 of July 20, 1961 later transferred civil defense functions to the Secretary of Defense. The text of the reorganization plan is not held; the held Federal Register text of Executive Order 10952 (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10952.txt, 26 FR 6577) does not name this order. Neither instrument names Executive Order 10222, and no held source shows that either extinguished its commands; the same 1989 Codification still printed the order as in force on January 20, 1989. Neither has an evidence record in this dossier, so each is disclosed here rather than recorded as a later event. Searches: I read the coverage notes of the three machine searches before selecting them. The U.S. Code search covers the release point current through 2026-10-09 (laws enacted from then through 2026-10-14 are not reflected) and the eCFR search runs as of 2026-10-14; both are complete with no coverage warning and serve here to show that no current provision gives this order continuing force after its revocation. The OFR disposition-note search records only the Executive Order 12919 supersession or revocation for this order. The held-text number search found this number only in the held texts of Executive Order 12919 and in the OFR 1989 Codification.

savings.reason: The transfers of functions, property, records and personnel made under the order are accrued effects of executed transfers. Section 903 of Executive Order 12919 provides that previously issued orders and other actions relating to any function it affects "shall remain in effect except as they are inconsistent with this order" or are later amended or revoked, and that "Nothing in this order shall affect the validity or force of anything done under previous delegations or other assignment of authority under the Act." The whole held text of Executive Order 12919 is cited as the savings source.
